content.thinking:
I'm working out the arc function signature and figuring out typing for the chain and joint structures, deciding to rely on inferred types rather than importing explicit ones where possible. Now I'm drafting the hand function signature and building out the composition carefully.

Still defining digit geometry... working out swing direction based on cross products to determine finger and thumb curl angles, spacing them along the axial direction, and placing the palm and wrist joints relative to the limb's radius and tip position.

For the limbs, I'm sweeping the forearm and thigh bones with tapering radii across keyframes, attaching fur and spheres at shoulder and elbow joints, and setting up the leg chain (hip, knee, ankle) parented to the hips with a "leg" role and contact behavior, while the arm chain parents to the spine's tip joint.

Now I'm working through the leg IK: the hind-limb solution needs a knee hint positioned forward and slightly outward depending on the model's left/right side, then creating the head joint parented to the neck with a forward-tilted direction, followed by setting up the jaw joint as a child of the head.

I'm also defining ear joints as hinges on the head, then building the skull as a low-poly sphere scaled to fit the head shape, deciding to keep smooth shading with low segment counts so the silhouette still reads as faceted and chunky for the pixel-art style.

Now I'm placing the muzzle as a cream sphere positioned and scaled against the head, sharing the same fur paint ramp, then adding the nose as a tiny dark box further forward with black cell-paint, and sketching out how to add pixel-dot nostrils via a decal texture near the nose tip.

For the eyes, I'm planning small decals, with a subtle darker ring around them to mimic the koala's faint eye markings, drafting a 5x5 pixel pattern where the outer ring uses a muted blue-grey and the center stays dark for the pupil, leaving transparent background pixels so the surrounding fur shows through.

For the mouth, I'm thinking through how to draw a philtrum line down from the nose and a V-shaped mouth line, considering whether to use thin rod geometry or drape a path along the muzzle surface, and starting to define the catmull-rom points for that curve.

Now I'm working out how the lower jaw should sit relative to the muzzle underside, adjusting the y-coordinates and scale of a sphere shape so it tucks beneath the muzzle bottom without excessive overlap.

With the mouth line roughly settled, I'm moving on to adding chin fur tufts and head fur cards on the cheeks, then planning to write out the whole file including stand fixtures. I'm also defining a tapered radius function for the branch sweep, setting up the sweep call with bone, color, sides, and cap styles, then planning sub-branches off the third back branch before adding leaf card details.

Now I'm placing leaf clusters at the branch tips and scattering mid-twigs, plus designing a forked knob sphere and a metal bracket collar at the trunk base using a lathed ring profile with bolt spheres around it. I'm also planning ground clutter -- fallen leaves, gumnuts, moss, and pebbles -- before writing the scatter logic for the base top surface.

I'm excluding the trunk base area from the scatter using a distance filter, and checking how flat color strings count toward the palette limit versus textures. I need to watch for unused imports causing TypeScript errors, and I'm writing the fur card generation function using surface scattering with a minimum distance and normal filter.

Setting up card colors for cheek tufts, arm cards, and inner-ear plating...

For the eyes, I'll mirror the left eye off the right using the sign on the x-axis, keeping highlights separate so they don't flip incorrectly. Now I'm ready to write out the full file.
